q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a plastic crate?
title: Plastic crate carbon footprint per crate
short: Multiply the crate's weight by your polymer supplier's per-kg figure for PP or HDPE. Add the moulding shop's electricity per kg, divided across crates passed, plus any printing and pallet wrap. Polymer is usually most of the total.
audience: Injection moulders making crates and returnable packaging

ul: PP copolymer or HDPE by crate weight.
Regrind share, which lowers the virgin polymer needed.
Injection moulding machines, the largest electricity user.

p: Give the crate weight with the figure. A returnable crate's footprint per trip is the crate figure divided by the trips it makes.

example.title: Worked example: moulding shop per crate (one month)
lines: Plant total: 85,200 / 200,000 = 0.426 kg CO2 per crate
Add the polymer per crate for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
